::: {.solutions}

Three printable pages. The Paper 1 sheet is the mathematics both papers assume; the Paper 2 sheet is the
reasoning vocabulary and the two topics that appear in every sitting.

| | Sheet | What it carries |
|---|---|---|
| **Paper 1** | **[Blank — fill it in yourself](paper1_formula_sheet_blank.qmd)** | the same headings with the formulas removed |
| **Paper 1** | **[Completed reference copy](paper1_formula_sheet.qmd)** | MM1–MM8 formulas, mini-examples, recurring question types, fast methods, and exam traps |
| **Paper 1** | **[Formula sheet + card challenges](paper1_formula_sheet_challenge.qmd)** | the full reference with one high-difficulty problem and inline solution toggle directly under every concept card |
| **Paper 1** | **[Formula-sheet worksheet and mark scheme](paper1_formula_sheet_ws.qmd)** | all 57 concept-card challenges with working space and fully visible English solutions |
| **Paper 2** | **[Formula sheet & concept summary](paper2_formula_sheet.qmd)** | S1–S7 reasoning, recurring topic engines, standard counterexamples, and an exam-day card |
| **Paper 2** | **[Formula sheet + card challenges](paper2_formula_sheet_challenge.qmd)** | the full reasoning reference with one high-difficulty problem and inline solution toggle under every concept card |

::: {.callout-tip}
## Use the blank one first

Writing a formula sheet from memory is worth more than reading one. Fill in
**[the blank copy](paper1_formula_sheet_blank.qmd)** cold, then open
**[the reference copy](paper1_formula_sheet.qmd)** and mark it. What you could not produce is your revision
list — not what you could not recognise.
:::

:::
